title: Data Scientist Salary USA 2026: Pay by Level and City
metaDescription: Data scientist salary USA 2026: median $120,230, entry $85K–$120K, senior $155K–$210K. Top cities, ML and AI premiums, plus a 34% job growth outlook.
headline: Data Scientist Salary USA 2026: Pay by Level, City and Skill

sections.title: 2026 salary bands: entry to principal
sections.content:
The median base salary for a data scientist in the United States sits near $120,230, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, with most credible sources placing the average between $120,000 and $128,000 in 2026. Entry-level data scientists earn roughly $85,000 to $120,000, and mid-level scientists with two to five years of experience earn $120,000 to $155,000.

Senior data scientists earn $155,000 to $210,000 in base salary, while staff and principal scientists earn $180,000 to $230,000 in base pay. Total compensation tells a bigger story: senior packages frequently clear $220,000, and top tech employers pay total compensation of $250,000 to $350,000 or more once equity is included.

sections.title: Pay by city: San Francisco, New York and Seattle
sections.content:
San Francisco and the Bay Area remain the ceiling, with average base pay around $172,000 and senior ranges reaching $160,000 to $225,000. New York and Seattle follow closely, and Boston, Austin and Washington DC also pay well above the national median. The catch is cost of living: a $200,000 salary in the Bay Area can feel like $130,000 elsewhere.

Remote roles exist, but pay is usually anchored to the employer's metro, so location still shapes the offer. Second-tier metros pay less in base salary but often deliver a better standard of living, and state-level averages vary widely, from under $110,000 in some states to well over $140,000 in California and New York.

sections.title: Specialisations that pay more: ML, AI and computer vision
sections.content:
Machine learning and AI specialisation carries the largest premium in 2026. Motion Recruitment reports that ML and AI specialists earn 15 to 30 percent more than generalists at the same experience level, with computer vision specialists at the top of published ranges. Deep learning, NLP and MLOps skills also lift pay, while Python, SQL and statistics remain the expected foundation for every role.

The biggest raises go to scientists who can show measurable business impact from their models, not just to those with the longest list of tools. Product sense, clear communication with non-technical stakeholders and experience deploying models to production are the differentiators that move a candidate from the middle of a band to the top of it.

sections.title: Demand outlook and how to reach the top bands
sections.content:
The outlook is very strong. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects data scientist employment to grow 34 percent between 2024 and 2034, among the fastest rates of any occupation, as every industry adopts AI and analytics. Demand is strongest for senior scientists and ML specialists, while entry-level generalists face heavy competition for a limited pool of junior roles.

The fastest route to the top bands is specialisation plus proof. A portfolio of deployed models with real business results, depth in one domain such as NLP or computer vision, and cloud and MLOps skills will beat a generic resume. Early-career scientists should pick a specialisation, ship real projects and learn to explain the business value of their work.
